root.name: Four Knights Game: Spanish Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bb5

overview: White pins the c6 knight, a symmetrical Spanish. Black replies 4...Nd4 (Rubinstein, 5.Nxd4 exd4 6.e5 dxc3 7.exf6 Qxf6 8.dxc3 for an equal queenless-leaning middlegame) or 4...Bb4 (Double Spanish, 5.O-O O-O 6.d3 d6 7.Bg5 Bxc3 8.bxc3 Qe7). The play is slow and balanced; White gets doubled c-pawns or a small initiative but the draw margin is wide.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with d3, Bg5 and Nd5, keep everything protected, and wait for errors.
Trade on c6 or c3 to damage Black's structure.

black_ideas.idea: Mirror White with ...Bb4 and ...O-O and trade down.
Play the Rubinstein with ...Nd4 for a different pawn structure.

typical_structures.structure: Symmetrical e4 against e5 with doubled c-pawns after Bxc3.

character.notes: Symmetrical and hard to break; drawish reputation. Solid.

structure.notes: Central tension left in place; flexible.

level.notes: Popular at club level because it needs little theory; I judge Intermediate, Beginner is possible.

sublines_that_differ.name: Rubinstein
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bb5 Nd4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black seeks a more unbalanced structure.

sublines_that_differ.name: Ranken
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bb5 a6 5. Bxc6
sublines_that_differ.how: White doubles Black's pawns at once.

level.reason: Little theory but plans need care.

plans.reason: Bxc3 and the symmetrical centre dominate.
